title: Mem

cards: Before there is light, before land, before anything has a name, there is water. That's how the Torah opens.
The earth is without form, darkness lies over the deep, and, in the King James, "the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters." Water isn't made on any of the days that follow.

It's simply there, waiting, at the very start of the story. And the Hebrew word for it is small and round, with a humming sound you make with closed lips: mayim. Today's letter opens it and closes it.

teach.b: Four sips. First, the word. Mayim is spelled mem, yud, mem: the letter at both ends, a little yud between, like water held in a cup.
Second, the shape. Mem changes with where it falls.
In the middle of a word it's open at the bottom, a mem you could pour out of. At the end of a word it closes into a square, sealed. Mayim uses both.

Some teachers like that picture: water that flows, and water that's held. Third, a name drawn out of water. In Exodus, a baby is hidden in a basket among the reeds of the river, and Pharaoh's daughter finds him.
In the King James: "And she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water." In Hebrew he's Moshe, and his name begins with mem.
The man who will one day lead the people through the sea begins his life lifted out of a river. Fourth, the cup in your hand. Even water gets a blessing.
Before drinking it, Jews who say blessings recite a short one praising God, by whose word all things came to be.
Not the blessing for wine, not the blessing for bread: a short, general one, for a plain drink. Water is easy to stop noticing.
The Torah puts it on the first page, and the blessing puts a pause before every glass.

how: Before drinking water, observant Jews say a short blessing, the shehakol, praising God 'by whose word all things came to be'; children learning to write Hebrew are taught the open mem and the closed final mem.

o: a letter shaped like a wave of the sea
the letter at both ends of mayim, water
the letter at both ends of Moshe's name

p: in the middle of a word
at the end of a word

s: in Genesis, water is created on one of the days
it's already there at the start: "the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters."
mayim has the open mem and the closed mem
it starts with the open form and ends with the closed, final one.
only wine and bread get a blessing

games.q: you're Pharaoh's daughter. you lifted a crying baby in a basket out of the river, and now the child has grown and is brought to you. what name do you give him, and why?
o: Moses, because I drew him out of the water.
a royal Egyptian name, to hide where he came from.
no name until his mother is found.
games.why: "she called his name Moses: and she said, Because I drew him out of the water." Moshe begins with mem.

practice: If a glass of water is near, pick it up; if not, keep this for the next one you drink. Look at it first, its weight in your hand and the light in it, then take one slow sip and follow it down, and let the next one take longer.
If you say blessings, this is a moment for the blessing over water; if you don't, let the glass be the whole of your attention.

wordCard.voice: Mem. The letter at both ends of mayim, water, open in the middle of a word and closed at the end. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: water. Open mem (מ) at the start, closed final mem (ם) at the end.

carryVoice: Your line: mem is water. Even a plain glass of water is worth noticing. Until tomorrow.
